transcript: In the basement of this new york city bar is an immersive theatrical experience where the motto is “eavesdropping mandatory” This weekend, I was invited to see Secrets Bar, where the actors intermingle with the audience as both employees and fellow patrons, and we listen in on their drama and titular secrets. They occasionally interact with us as well, sometimes asking for advice or help with their problems, and sometimes trying to coax out some secrets of our own. I have a broken finger right now, and one of the actors asked if I f*ng*red someone too hard, which I thought was hilarious and probably my favourite moment of the experience. Audience participation is pretty limited, though. Mostly you're sitting in your seat watching the action happen around you, and mostly there's a pretty clear point of focus where they use lighting and microphones to direct your attention around the space to whatever scene is happening at that time. And for some audience members, that's gonna be ideal. Personally, I think for an immersive, interactive experience like this, I might have liked for them to make the audience work a little harder to put the pieces together of the various storylines happening simultaneously, maybe to the point where we can even kind of choose our own adventure of which storylines to follow more closely, so that we really feel like we're playing an active role in essentially invading these people's privacy. Again, if you're more new to the world of interactive or immersive theatre or only like very light audience interaction, This could be a perfect option for you. For me it came across a bit more like a prototype or a proof of concept, but I still find the format pretty inventive and there's definitely a sense of fun to watching the action unfold like a cheesy soap opera, especially when the promise of juicy gossip is fulfilled.
